sections.title: Tent Poles — Memory Layer with Tools + Dashboard

todos.content: Design and document the Tent Poles memory layer: collaborative context compaction where Jasper proposes key load-bearing points (tent poles), user reviews/prioritizes, approved tent poles replace old messages. Concept doc with data structure, flow, storage, tools, UI, and open questions.
todos.notes: Concept designed. Tent poles = structural key points (decisions, facts, preferences, open questions, constraints). User co-creates and prioritizes. Replaces narrative summarization with collaborative context curation.

todos.content: Choose and implement storage layer for tent poles. Option A: JSON file + sidecar endpoint (like todos.json pattern, proven, survives restarts). Option B: LangGraph Store with semantic search (proper integration, cross-thread, but dev server Store is in-memory with hot-reload issue). QUESTION: Which storage approach?
todos.notes: Open question: JSON file vs LangGraph Store. JSON is safer given hot-reload persistence issue. Store is better long-term for cross-thread semantic search. Consider JSON now, migrate to Store for production.

todos.content: Convert Jasper from single-node plain LLM call to ReAct agent loop with ToolNode. Required for tent pole tools AND for the search/code-viz tools. Steps: define @tool functions, bind_tools on LLM, add ToolNode, conditional edge (tool_calls → ToolNode, else END), bridge message formats at subgraph boundary. This is foundational — enables all tool-using features.
todos.notes: Infrastructure change. Same ReAct pattern needed for search tools (Tavily/Exa) and code viz tools (Tree-sitter/Code2flow/Mermaid). Build once, reuse for all tools.

todos.content: Define LangChain @tool functions for tent pole management: propose_tent_poles (Jasper identifies from conversation, presents for review), set_tent_pole (add with priority), update_tent_pole (edit/reprioritize), remove_tent_pole (drop), get_tent_poles (read current set). Tools read/write storage layer.
todos.notes: propose_tent_poles is the collaborative moment — Jasper reviews conversation, extracts load-bearing points, user reviews. Other tools maintain tent poles as conversation evolves.

todos.content: Build tent poles dashboard UI. QUESTION: Where should it live? Option A: third sidebar panel or tab in existing right sidebar (consistent with todo pattern). Option B: collapsible horizontal bar above chat (always visible, limited space). Option C: separate /dashboard route (most powerful, context switch). Option D: artifact panel (reuses existing, tied to messages). Also needs: pending review indicator, inline edit, drag-to-reorder, approve/reject buttons.
todos.notes: Open question: dashboard location. Consider: right sidebar already has Todos — could add Tent Poles as a second tab. Horizontal bar is always visible but cramped. Separate page is powerful but disconnected from chat.

todos.content: Decide: Are tent poles per-thread or global? Per-thread means each conversation has its own set. Global means tent poles persist across conversations building a knowledge base over time. QUESTION: Which scope? Hybrid possible — global tent poles with per-thread overrides.
todos.notes: Open question: scope. Global enables cross-conversation memory (user preferences, project facts). Per-thread keeps conversations independent. Hybrid: global facts + per-thread decisions.

todos.content: Implement trigger logic for tent pole proposal. QUESTION: When should Jasper offer? Automatic at threshold (20+ messages)? Jasper notices it's losing track? User-triggered + auto-offer? User-triggered only? User said Jasper should ask and invite review — collaborative, not silent.
todos.notes: Open question: trigger. User intent: 'Jasper will ask and invite the user to review the summary to support shared understanding.'倾向于自动提议 + 用户可随时触发.

todos.content: Implement context compaction: after user approves tent poles, replace old messages with tent poles as structured context block + keep recent 6-8 exchanges. Add trim_history() to agent_utils.py using langchain_core trim_messages with count_tokens_approximately, strategy='last'. Per-agent max_tokens: Jasper 4000, OpenCode 8000, Research 6000, Supervisor 2000.
todos.notes: Fixes context window overflow that causes Jasper to lose memory. trim_messages from LangGraph docs. Per-agent limits let each agent choose its memory budget.

todos.content: Stop LangGraph dev server hot-reload from killing in-memory checkpoints. Add --no-reload flag or configure in langgraph.json. Dev server uses langgraph_runtime_inmem._persistence with periodic flush to .langgraph_api/*.pckl. Hot-reload stops flush loop, loses unsaved checkpoints. Logs show '3 changes detected' every 10 seconds.
todos.notes: Root cause of Jasper losing memory mid-conversation. The dev server hot-reloads on file changes, wiping in-memory checkpoints before they're flushed to disk.

Candidates researched: Tavily (iterative /research, spam filter, langchain-tavily), Exa (neural, docs/code focus, powers Cursor, langchain-exa), Jina Reader (URL→markdown, free tier). sections.title: UI Performance — Slow/Freeze Diagnosis and Fix Plan

todos.content: Diagnose and document root causes of UI slowness and freezing during agent responses. Three root causes identified: (1) No throttle on stream state updates — every LLM token triggers immediate React re-render. (2) MarkdownText re-parses entire accumulated content on every render — ReactMarkdown with remarkGfm + remarkMath + rehypeKatex is expensive per render. (3) onCustomEvent handler adds 'custom' to streamMode for ALL requests including Jasper — server sends custom events even when no agent emits them, adding SSE overhead.
todos.notes: Root causes found via LangGraph SDK source code analysis. StreamManager (manager.js) processes every token: messages.slice() copies full array, creates new state object, calls notifyListeners. With throttle:50 added, renders batched but state mutations still run per-token. callbackStreamMode (stream.lgp.js:146) auto-adds 'custom' mode when onCustomEvent is set — overhead on every request.

todos.content: Add throttle:50 to useTypedStream options in Stream.tsx. Batches React re-renders to max once per 50ms instead of every token. Applied — verify it helps with fast cloud models.
todos.notes: Added to Stream.tsx:112. Throttle batches renders but not state mutations. SDK source: StreamManager.subscribe (manager.js:287) uses setTimeout to defer listener calls. Helps but does not solve the core issue of per-token object creation.

todos.content: Consider increasing throttle from 50ms to 100-200ms. Reduces render frequency from 20fps to 5-10fps. Still smooth for reading streaming text but halves markdown re-parse cost. Simple one-line change in Stream.tsx.
todos.notes: Trade-off: higher throttle = less CPU but choppier text appearance. 150ms is a good middle ground. Test with fast cloud model to find sweet spot.

todos.content: Remove the onCustomEvent 'text' handler in Stream.tsx:128-129. Currently calls options.mutate() for every OpenCode text chunk, setting opencode_status='streaming' hundreds of times per second. The 'text' events are already streamed via messages stream mode. Only keep handlers for 'status', 'complete', 'error' events.
todos.notes: The 'text' custom event handler is redundant — text chunks arrive via messages stream mode. The mutate() call creates unnecessary state objects per token. Removing it eliminates per-token state mutation overhead during OpenCode runs.

todos.content: Memoize MarkdownText component more aggressively. Only render full markdown when message streaming is complete. During streaming, show raw text. When streaming completes, render parsed markdown. This eliminates per-render markdown re-parse during streaming.
todos.notes: MarkdownText is already wrapped in memo() but children (content string) change every token during streaming. Approach: add a 'streaming' prop, render plain text when streaming=true, switch to ReactMarkdown when streaming=false. Requires passing isLoading state to message components.

todos.content: Lazy-load remarkMath and rehypeKatex plugins in markdown-text.tsx. These are heavy and most messages contain no math. Load them only when LaTeX delimiters ($...$, $$...$$) are detected in content. Reduces initial parse cost for non-math messages significantly.
todos.notes: katex.min.css and rehype-katex are expensive. Conditional loading: check content for math delimiters before passing plugins to ReactMarkdown. Could use React.lazy or dynamic import for the plugins.

todos.content: Add langsmith:nostream tag to cloud models that stream too fast. Per Agent Chat UI README: .with_config({tags:['langsmith:nostream']}) prevents live token streaming. Response appears all at once after completion. Eliminates per-token overhead entirely. Toggle per model: use nostream for fast cloud models, allow streaming for local models.
todos.notes: Trade-off: no live feedback (user waits for full response) but zero freeze risk. Best for cloud models with high token throughput. The tag is checked by the LangGraph server — it suppresses on_chat_model_stream events for tagged models. Source: Agent Chat UI README 'Hiding Messages' section.

todos.content: Only poll /api/todos when the todo sidebar is open. Currently TodoList component polls every 3s regardless of visibility. The motion.div hides it with CSS but the component stays mounted and polling. Add a visibility check or conditionally mount/unmount based on todosOpen state.
todos.notes: TodoList is always mounted inside motion.div (index.tsx:392). Even when sidebar is closed (x:300, off-screen), useEffect interval runs every 3s, calling fetch + setSections. This adds render pressure during streaming. Fix: pass todosOpen as prop, only set interval when open.

todos.content: Only add 'custom' to streamMode when the target agent is OpenCode. Currently callbackStreamMode always includes 'custom' because onCustomEvent is always set. Could split onCustomEvent into two: one for UIMessage (always), one for OpenCode status (conditional). Or conditionally set onCustomEvent based on selectedAgent.
todos.notes: The SDK auto-adds 'custom' to stream mode when onCustomEvent != null (stream.lgp.js:146). This means even Jasper requests get 'custom' in streamMode. The server then sends custom events (none for Jasper) adding SSE parsing overhead. Fix: only register the OpenCode status handler when routing to OpenCode.
